record.title: Bring HHP-Lab source architecture to a generally coherent state
record.rationale: HHP-Lab has a sound domain-oriented foundation, but implicit dependency direction, import cycles, oversized coordination modules, and inconsistent adapter boundaries make the structure harder to extend safely.

scope.statement: Production Python source organization and its architectural governance.
exclusions: Renaming published artifacts solely for structural symmetry

intent.statement: The source tree has understandable ownership and dependency direction, with obvious structural problems resolved.
intent.rationale: The cleanup should reach a maintainable stopping point rather than pursue theoretical perfection.

intent.statement: Architectural cleanup must not silently change reproducible outputs, schemas, provenance, CLI behavior, or canonical artifact names.
intent.rationale: Replication and result stability take precedence over cosmetic restructuring.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Architecture review finds no unresolved high-confidence layer violation, known multi-file import cycle, or unowned cross-cutting responsibility.

expectation.decision_rule: Elements reconciliation and a focused source review find no obvious structural defect left without either resolution or a documented exception.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Existing supported workflows retain their observable contracts.

expectation.decision_rule: Relevant tests and artifact contract checks pass without unreviewed changes to schemas, names, provenance, or reported-result behavior.

record.title: Standardize external-source adapter boundaries
record.rationale: External data sources should vary in source-specific acquisition and parsing while sharing operational policy for snapshots, normalization, validation, provenance, registries, and persistence.

scope.statement: ACS, Census, HUD, BLS, CDC, Vera, MEDSL, PRISM, NHGIS, and future external-source ingestion.
exclusions: Forcing source-specific semantics into a lowest-common-denominator abstraction

intent.statement: Each external source follows an explicit adapter pipeline from source specification through acquisition, normalization, validation, provenance, and canonical persistence.
intent.rationale: A consistent extension boundary makes new sources easier to add and audit.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Adding a representative source primarily requires a focused adapter and registry entry rather than edits to a central monolithic workflow.

expectation.decision_rule: Architecture review confirms shared operational stages and source-owned acquisition or parsing implementations.

record.title: Remove known multi-file production dependency cycles
record.rationale: Five credible file-level cycles cross CLI initialization, recipe execution, metro I/O, covariate processing, and ACS or crosswalk responsibilities.

scope.statement: The five production cycles currently reported by elements-rust.

intent.statement: Production module initialization and direct module dependencies are acyclic for the currently known cycle set.
intent.rationale: Acyclic ownership improves import safety and makes dependency direction legible.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The five baselined production cycles no longer appear.

expectation.decision_rule: A fresh Elements scaffold followed by production cycle analysis reports none of the CLI, recipe, metro, covariate, or ACS-crosswalk cycles.

record.title: Decompose oversized coordination hubs into focused modules
record.rationale: Several modules combine dispatch, transformation, persistence, and policy, increasing change blast radius and obscuring responsibility.

scope.statement: Naming, covariate ingestion and aggregation, recipe execution, and reusable results-workflow logic.
exclusions: Splitting files solely to meet a line-count threshold
Removing thin named workflows needed for reproducibility

intent.statement: Large coordination modules delegate to cohesive components with clear ownership while retaining stable public facades where useful.
intent.rationale: Decomposition should reduce coupling without forcing a disruptive caller migration.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Target hubs primarily coordinate rather than contain multiple source-specific or artifact-family implementations.

expectation.decision_rule: Review of naming, covariates, recipe execution, and results workflows finds focused implementation modules and no new compatibility regression.

record.title: Make architectural layers and dependency direction explicit
record.rationale: The repository is organized by domain but currently has no declared layer model, allowing dependency inversions to accumulate unnoticed.

scope.statement: Production packages and automated architectural checks.
exclusions: Exhaustively classifying every helper before useful enforcement begins

intent.statement: Interfaces depend on application orchestration, which depends on domain services and stable contracts or infrastructure through reviewed directions.
intent.rationale: A small explicit model is sufficient to prevent new architectural drift.

intent.statement: Lower-level domain, contract, and infrastructure code must not depend on CLI or report entry points.
intent.rationale: Entry-point dependencies make reusable logic sensitive to initialization and presentation concerns.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Elements represents the reviewed layer model and can report coverage and violations.

expectation.decision_rule: The repository has declared architectural intent for its major layers and automated checks reject newly introduced forbidden dependency directions.

record.title: Keep cross-cutting contracts narrow and stable
record.rationale: Paths, naming, schema columns, package facades, and geographic definitions have broad reach and therefore require especially clear dependency and API boundaries.

scope.statement: High-fan-in shared policy and contract modules.
exclusions: Treating high fan-in itself as a defect
Duplicating canonical constants to reduce graph metrics

intent.statement: Cross-cutting modules expose narrow stable contracts and remain below workflow and domain orchestration.
intent.rationale: Stable low-level policy modules can legitimately have many consumers without becoming architectural grab bags.

intent.statement: Package initializers must not own substantial implementation or create initialization cycles through broad re-exports.
intent.rationale: Passive facades reduce hidden import behavior and cycle risk.

acceptance_criteria.statement: High-fan-in modules have documented ownership and no upward or cyclic dependency.

expectation.decision_rule: Elements graphs and source review show narrow dependencies for paths, naming, schema, definitions, and package initializers.
